title: Integral Donovan Finiteness over Witt Vectors
main_claim: For every prime p and bound M, blocks of finite groups over W(F_p-bar) with defect groups of order at most M fall into finitely many O-linear Morita classes. The defect groups may be nonabelian and p=2 is included. The paper also extends this to any fixed complete DVR of characteristic 0 with algebraically closed residue field.

issues.location: Sec 2, paragraph after Prop 2.3; Thm 5.3 'Transport from arbitrary subgroups'
issues.description: A non-pure p-subgroup S of Q=Stab_Y(bbar) is conjugated by chi in Xi into X. The conjugate stabilizes chi(bbar), not bbar. Prop 4.2 and Prop 5.2 are stated only for S <= Q ∩ X with the fixed block bbar. The paper only asserts that the transported block stays 'in the same family'. It does not explicitly re-run the comparison and the Gamma_S construction for chi(bbar).
issues.evidence: chi(bbar) is another block of O Nbar covering b, because chi acts trivially on O N. Prop 2.3(ii) bounds the defect of every block covering b, and the companion's comparison works for any such block. So this is an omitted routine step, not a failure.

coverage:
I read all seven sections in full, along with the companion's Sec 9 (Lemmas 9.5 and 9.7 and the proof of Prop 9.1). Checks, step by step:
(1) Integral orbit lemma 3.1: the unit minor from Smith normal form; the generic dimension bound and the special-fibre dimension bound via Stacks 0B2J; dense orbits in u-dimensional components; Hensel slice and isolated points.
(2) Lemma 3.2: HH^1(OG)=0 via Shapiro, and finiteness of Out via the orbit lemma.
(3) Thm 3.3: the grading tangent calculation. Cancellation in H gives a derivation, and the argument never divides by |H|.
(4) Prop 3.5: rank bound giving finitely many isomorphism types, and the marking count.
(5) Sec 4: the overlap scalars D_ad(l) = lambda_m(l)^{-1} E_l. I re-derived these from f(l^{-1}) = lambda_m(l) l^{-1}. The presentation and central ambiguities lie in T, lambda_m(c)=1 on central p-elements, the 2-cocycle identity holds, and H^2(S,T)=0.
(6) Lemma 5.1, Marcus-type extension: well-definedness and the factor law.
(7) Prop 5.2: the group Gamma_S, b̄ is a block of Gamma_S, the defect bound, mf ≤ m, and the use of EEL Thm 3.10.
(8) Thm 6.3: K-scalars reduce to beta in T; z_k in T via a homomorphism K → U_R; E splits as a product of M_n(O) with p ∤ n; orbit corners have the form M_n ⊗ C_j. I re-derived the product formula for w_s w_t, and det c_s = 1 forces gamma into mu_n ⊆ T. The H^2 torsor argument and the finite kernel of restriction (cor∘res on U_R, and H^2(Q,T) finite) also check out.
(9) Assembly and Cor 1.2: base change of Morita contexts and uniqueness of central idempotent lifts.
Not independently verified (black boxes): EEL Thm 3.10, An–Eaton Prop 6.1, the companion's Lemmas 8.1–8.5 and 9.2–9.6 (structure, dual recovery, Bonnafé–Rouquier hypotheses, bounded Frobenius return), and Eisele's Picard finiteness.
sibling_notes: Sibling (rank 127, the field companion) also reported no_gap_found. The main thing this paper adds is the T-valued refinement of the companion's scalar errors: the companion only proves exactness mod p. I checked the refinement against companion Lemma 9.7, and it holds over O because lambda_m has p'-order and the central p'-character ratios are roots of unity. Shared residual risk: EEL Thm 3.10 and the companion's Lie-type constructions.
